# R331 — fixed-history full-logit artifact and comparator contract

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only source and report audit of W at `e3c904e2e2247826f758ef0e682e2e7051152b86`. Consulted R318, R319, R323, registry v176 (836 completed reports), relevant current CLI/source and extant scoring scripts. No project execution, import, test, build, device/model/profiler/process work, Git operation, cleanup, or source change. This is a source-level feasibility finding, not runtime qualification or a quality result.

## Finding

For the standalone native-pack route, `--spec-follow` plus `--dump-logits` already provides a fixed-history full-vocabulary capture on the production prompt-prefill plus verifier/commit path. A CPU-side comparator can calculate paired target-token NLL/PPL, full-vocabulary KL, top-1/top-2 and target ranks/margins from existing dumps; no new inference code is necessary for that standalone comparison. Existing comparator scripts demonstrate useful metric calculations, but none in current W is a trustworthy drop-in contract for the current native row convention: the artifact carries only dimensions and floats, and the old scripts either assume another row alignment or silently truncate mismatched dumps. The narrow gap is a strict CPU comparator/metadata contract, not a general-purpose new inference API.

This path measures the standalone native route. It does not certify `--serve`, API behavior, runtime qualification on any target, end-task quality, or quiet performance. Free-running prose equality is not a quality criterion: `--spec-follow` intentionally substitutes the requested continuation for model predictions.

## Artifact layout and row/target mapping

The `--dump-logits` binary begins with two native-endian int32 values, `{vocab_size, row_count}`, followed by row-major float32 raw logits. There is no magic/version, tokenizer/model identity, token IDs, position array, dtype tag, or route metadata in the file itself. Row order is emission order. Full coverage requires the default `--logits-stride 1`; stride selection is zero-based multiples plus the final input position, and strides above one are restricted to `--max-new 1`.

For native prompt length (P) and fixed continuation length (N), the native-pack path captures from prompt token `P-1` onward. Row `i) is the distribution after processing prompt token `P-1` (for i=0) or fixed continuation token `i-1` (for i>0); it predicts fixed target continuation ID `i`. Its absolute predictor position is `P-1+i`. Full-history scoring therefore requires (N) rows, with target IDs `follow[0..N-1]`, at positions `P-1 .. P+N-2`. The batched prompt handles the preceding (P-1) IDs; the last prompt ID is processed in the first verifier window. Existing standalone verifier commit logic only commits the contiguous proposed prefix matching the forced continuation, preserving the causal KV/GDN/PLE history for later rows.

The header row count is initialized from `max_new` for a native pack. The follow file bounds the loop to `min(max_new, follow.size())`; an empty/missing follow falls back to ordinary output behavior, and a too-short follow silently produces fewer than the requested (N) targets. A fixed-history recipe should therefore use exactly N follow IDs and `--max-new N`, reject N=0, and verify `produced == N), dump rows == N, and exact file size `8 + 4 * vocab_size * N`. At `P+N-1 > max_context`, the full requested position set is outside the configured context capacity and must be rejected or split under an explicitly defined context policy.

The standalone default leaves `stop_eos` off; if `--stop-eos` is enabled, a forced EOS can end capture before N rows. For an exact N-token corpus continuation, require it off unless early EOS is explicitly the target truncation policy, and require the observed row count to agree with that policy. The scoring comparator must use the tokenizer's actual reference IDs and explicit masking/BOS rules; a vocabulary dimension alone cannot establish tokenization equivalence.

The bounded atomics-safe native verifier route is the R323 condition: set `STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1` before launch and hold the remaining qualified route settings fixed. This forces segment completion before host reads and avoids the unsegmented concurrent volatile polling branch by source. It is a source-path fact, not proof that a run executed successfully or that a device/runtime was qualified. A quality capture is separate from timing because copying and writing every vocabulary row adds substantial overhead.

## Forced-history and operational prerequisites

- Use the same prompt ID sequence and same continuation ID sequence for baseline and candidate; record hashes and tokenizer/model artifact identity out of band. Keep max context, prompt batching, cache/residency, expert routing, device/runtime, and other arithmetic-affecting options aligned if the intended question is a paired kernel comparison.
- `--spec-follow` forces emitted output IDs and reports how many differ from the model argmax. That count is a prediction-divergence diagnostic only. It neither shows that all input history was correctly scored nor proves quality. The accepted-prefix rule plus exact row/target coverage is the causal-history contract.
- For the no-MTP standalone setup, `--spec-oracle` can supply the same continuation as drafts, reducing wasted windows; without oracle drafts the fallback proposal may be token 0. This is a performance of the quality capture only, not an acceptance requirement. If MTP is used, freeze its artifact/settings across arms; its draft route is distinct and must not be conflated with a no-MTP comparison.
- Require successful process completion and normal close, no relevant device/queue/kernel fault, complete stdout/stderr/receipt ownership, and evidence the logits file was closed successfully (`generate` prints an error and returns failure if `fclose` fails). Require exact output length and dimensions. Keep these operational checks separate from the numerical score.
- The verifier's `read_logits` copies rows but does not itself scan the whole vocabulary for finite values. `note_nonfinite` runs only when the nonfinite guard is enabled. Regardless, the comparator must scan every captured float and fail closed on NaN/Inf before computing any metric; a good mean or finite selected target cannot hide a bad tail row.
- Preserve capture hashes/metadata, input IDs or secure exact-history references, positions, row coverage and fault/status results. Use raw dumps only for a named comparison consumer and retire them when paired metrics are validated under the artifact-retention policy.

## Existing CPU comparator coverage

The project search found two directly relevant scripts plus other older first-logit utilities:

- `bench/results/2026-09-27-esp/esp_kl.py` loads the same 8-byte `int32 vocab, rows` header and float32 row matrix, computes double-precision log-softmax, forward KL, top-1 agreement and target-token NLL/PPL. It also launches an older per-token path on Windows and aligns targets as `ids[r+1]`. Reuse its stable metric pattern only after adapting alignment to the current native convention (row 0 target is follow[0], not a blind next-token index into a full token file).
- `bench/results/2026-09-30-xe-iq3xxs/window_logits.py` compares raw row logits, argmax agreement, and top-two margins, but only through first argmax divergence and does not score target NLL, KL, or artifact coverage.
- The old utilities do not carry or validate per-row position/target IDs, do not enforce complete paired row coverage, and one takes the minimum length of both files and the IDs. That truncation can make an incomplete/misaligned dump look comparable. No current `tools/logits_identical.py` exists in W despite a stale source comment naming it.

Thus a new CPU-only comparator can compute the requested metrics from existing dumps without any model import or inference code. It must not silently min-align or infer metadata from filename. Minimum strict contract: take both dump paths plus explicit matching prompt/follow IDs or their content hashes, `P,N,max_context`, tokenizer/model identifiers, and row-position convention; validate two-int32 header, same vocabulary and N rows, exact byte size, finite values, exact position and target coverage, and successful run/receipt statuses; then emit per-position target NLL/logprob delta, aggregate mean NLL and exp(mean NLL) PPL, forward/reverse KL direction labels, top-1 agreement, top-two margin and fixed-target rank summaries, with quantiles and artifact hashes. Use float64 log-sum-exp/accumulation. For PPL, use identical target masking, BOS and EOS policy in both arms. Full-vocabulary KL is available because the rows contain all logits; top-K or API logprobs alone would not recover tail mass.

This is a narrowly scoped comparator/ledger item, not approval to run a quality capture or promote a kernel. R318's calibration and task-level acceptance policy still applies: distributions on a fixed history are numerical evidence, while held-out task quality and operational correctness remain separate decisions. There is no universal acceptable KL/NLL/PPL margin.
